what: One image that Robot Lantern's builder cuts into a two-part 3D-printed ornament: a stencil sheet in one colour laid on a base in another. Red marks the stencil sheet; white is everything else.

make.with: an image model (GPT Image, Gemini, Midjourney or similar), from the customer's photo, as one new picture
make.ifNoImageModel: stop: don't draw it with code or SVG; send the customer to the product page to add their photo, and we make the drawing
make.handOver: the image exactly as the image model made it: save that file, or show it to the customer to download; never redraw it because the file couldn't be found
never: trace or threshold the photo with code
draw it as SVG or shapes
resize, recolour, sharpen or otherwise edit the generated image with code
make.ifItBreaksARule: generate a new image; don't fix it with code. If several were made, pick the one that keeps the likeness best and breaks no rule

file.normalisedBy: us, in the customer's browser: squared to 1024 x 1024; every pixel more than 120 (RGB distance) from white becomes ink (#E01010), the rest white
file.note: PNG is best; JPEG blurs the edges

colours.rule: exactly two flat colours: no grey, shading, gradients, texture or a third colour

composition.noFrame: no frame, border, box or background shape: the subject's own outline is the edge of the red
composition.scaledTo: the red is scaled to fit a box 80 mm wide and 85 mm tall, so a tall drawing prints narrower

style.look: bold poster stencil or linocut: the subject mostly solid red, its features as white cut-outs
style.onePiece: all the red is one connected shape: no floating dots, strokes or islands, and nothing red inside a white cut-out; join a detail that would float to its neighbour with a short red bridge
style.filledCutouts: every white cut-out is a filled white shape; never a thin white line round a red shape
style.outline: a continuous red border runs all the way round the outside, so the outer edge is one closed shape
style.fewShapes: few, chunky shapes; eyes are bold shapes, not dots; fur, hair and freckles are a few bold shapes
style.eyes: bold filled shapes: a white eye with a solid red pupil, or a solid red eye in a white socket; never a thin outline or a tiny dot

subjects.draw: the pet's head and the top of its neck only, keeping its likeness, markings and expression exactly
subjects.several: draw only the one whose head is largest and nearest the centre

subjects.draw: the person's head, hair and the top of the neck, plus anything worn on the head, keeping the likeness, face shape, hair and expression exactly; never change the expression
subjects.several: draw only the one whose face is largest and nearest the centre
subjects.consent: the customer has the person's OK; for a child, the customer is their parent or guardian or has one's OK

readyMade: the ready-made designs in product.json need no drawing: order one by its id on the product page
never: text, letters or numbers (the name goes on a separate tag)
cartoon or film characters, or other people's artwork
anything the customer doesn't have the right to use

printed.note: at 80 mm wide, 2% of a 1024 px image is about 1.6 mm; the builder drops red specks under 2 mm2, thickens red thinner than 1 mm and fills white gaps thinner than 1 mm, so thinner detail is lost or merged

refused: not PNG, JPEG or WebP; over 4 MB; not square (within 2%); under 1024 or over 4096 px; or transparent
looks like a photo or shaded art (more than 6% of pixels between ink and white)
fills the whole image (a frame, a background box, or the subject cut off by the edges), or one shape covers more than 80% of the image
no features: less than 3% of the shape cut out
more than one piece after the builder's cleanup, with an island more than 3 mm from the rest at print size, or more than 60 loose pieces
white kept under 0.8: the cleanup would fill in so much of the white that features the customer saw disappear (thin white lines are the usual cause)
warned: soft edges or light shading (made exactly two colours)
the art touching the edge of the image
the art under half the image width (scaled up, so it may print rougher)
the ink isn't red (it still prints in the stencil colour the customer chooses)
checks.where: the page runs these checks in the browser before anything is sent, and says what's wrong in words; the same builder runs again after payment

instructionsTested: spec v5 (2026-11-19): 9 stand-in photos, a usable drawing from every one, 67% of single tries usable
